features.title: How to use SPI protocol in bootloader on STM32 MCUs Introduction This application note describes the SPI protocol used in the STM32 microcontroller

caption: Table 2. SPI bootloader commands
rows: Gets the version and allowed commands supported by the current version of the bootloader.
Reads up to 256 bytes of memory starting from an address specified by the application.
Jumps to user application code located in the internal flash memory.
Writes up to 256 bytes to the memory starting from an address specified by the application.
Erases from one to all the flash memory pages or sectors using two-byte addressing mode.
Generic command that allows to add new features depending on the product constraints, without adding a new command for every feature.
Generic command that allows the user to send more data compared to the Special command.
Enables write protection for some sectors.
Disables write protection for all flash memory sectors.
Computes a CRC value on a given memory area with a size multiple of 4 bytes.

_notes: 1. If a denied command is received or an error occurs during command execution, the bootloader sends an NACK byte, and goes back to command checking.

caption: Table 3. Bootloader protocol versions
section: 3 Evolution of the bootloader protocol versions
rows: – Updated the Acknowledge mechanism. – Updated the "Get", "Get ID", "Get Version" and "Read" commands.
– Added support for "Get Checksum" command. – Updated "Get Command" command to return the opcode of the "Get Checksum" command.
– The number of commands can vary on STM32 devices with the same protocol version v2.0. To know the supported commands, use Get command.
